headline: Going Commando’s USA v1.01 matched code rises from 66.51% to 84.74%
summary: Five matching pull requests landed, taking Going Commando’s USA v1.01 from 66.51% to 84.74% of its code by size, with 7,760 of 8,579 functions matched. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. The other releases have their own figures: #386 reports USA v2.00 rising from 50.40% to 80.93% of code, with 7,586 of 8,634 functions, and Europe/Australia from 22.85% to 54.14%, with 6,992 of 8,672 functions.
highlights: The largest batch covers the lock-on tether family and two compiler fixes (#386). Its USA v1.01 figures precede the final daily progress report.
#384 adds 453 USA v1.01 functions across boot and level code. #385 adds three matches while retaining near-miss notes.
Yeedil and Aranos Prison gain 13 matched functions, alongside a fix for PAL and USA v2.00 (#387).
`func_00292078` matches at all 28 USA v1.01 placements, with release-specific handling corrected for USA v2.00 (#388).
Draft #389 holds functional C for the native port. It has not merged, is excluded from the matching build and adds no matches to the progress report.
